newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 30.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Government lifted the wraps on planned legislation which will make the eviction of hundreds of thousands of farm workers more difficult, and will make certain farm evictions are unlawful unless alternative accommodation is provided.

- The long-awaited unbundling of Malbak moved into high gear on Wednesday with news that controlling shareholder Sankorp had made an indicative bid for Malbak Motor Holdings and Swedish appliance manufacturer Electrolux had made an offer for Defy.
- In another blow to the SA Broadcasting Corporation's analogue pay television operation AstraSat, planned Afrikaans satellite television channel PrimaSat has opted to launch without the SABC.

- Grindrod Unicorn (Grincor), the Durban-based shipping, transport and investment group, lifted attributable income 38 percent to 54.5 million rand in the year to December after trading conditions improved and it received a healthy fillip from the rand's depreciation.
BUSINESS REPORT
- A massive fertiliser complex that could cost as much as 3.8 billion rand is to be built in Richards Bay, Foskor, the Phalaborwa-based phosphate producer, said.

- South Africa's largest black empowerment information technology deal was struck between Cisco, US-based supplier of network hardware, and the Consolidated Empowerment Initiative (CEIN), a company launched last month by seven black-owned computer companies.

- The Legal Resources Centre (LRC) is considering bringing a civil suit against Eskom, the state-owned electricity generator, for environmental pollution in Mpumalanga province, a spokesman from the centre said.
- Energy Africa and Soekor are working around the clock to free their oil production platform, Orca, after the vessel was "arrested" earlier this week by the sheriff of Simon's Town.
SAKE BEELD
- The government expects that half a million subsidies for cheap houses will be granted by June.
- The Gauteng government announced yesterday that casino licences in Gauteng should be granted.
- Cisco systems, one of the largest international network, made a deal with a group of black owned companies.
THE STAR
- Only two days after Sanelle Nkosi, 3, was admitted to an unregistered creche in Crystal Park, Benoni, his body was pulled from the swimming pool at the back of the house.
- Just a few days before women can get legal abortions on request, several Gauteng state hospitals and clinics are being inundated with queries about the service, staff said.
- A Parktown, Johannesburg, domestic worker was mauled to death by two pitbull terriers belonging to her employers.
